title: The model answers 429
heading: Symptom
text:
The model answers 429 › Symptom
A call to the model fails with HTTP 429 and the message "You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details". The message is the same whether the per-minute limit or the daily cap was hit, so the words alone do not tell you which one it is.

title: The model answers 429
heading: Tell the two apart
text:
The model answers 429 › Tell the two apart
Read the structured error details, not the message. A `QuotaFailure` entry names the quota that ran out in its `quotaId`. If the id contains `PerMinute`, the minute is not over yet. If it contains `PerDay`, the key's daily allowance is used up and no amount of waiting will help before midnight Pacific time. A `RetryInfo` entry carries a `retryDelay` such as `17s`: that is how long the provider asks you to wait.

title: The model answers 429
heading: Per-minute limit
text:
The model answers 429 › Per-minute limit
Wait as long as `retryDelay` says, plus one second, and send the request again. The retry helper in `src/system/plumbing.py` does this for you and gives up after fifteen minutes of continuous rate limiting, because at that point something other than the per-minute limit is wrong.

title: The model answers 429
heading: Daily cap
text:
The model answers 429 › Daily cap
Stop the run. Everything recorded so far is kept. Rerun the same command tomorrow, or with a partner's key, and it continues where it stopped. Do not create a second key on the same account to get around the cap: the cap is per project, and a second key shares it.

title: Rotate the model key
heading: When to rotate
text:
Rotate the model key › When to rotate
Rotate the Gemini key when it has been pasted anywhere it should not have been: a chat message, a screenshot, a commit, a classmate's laptop. Also rotate it at the end of every semester.

title: Rotate the model key
heading: Steps
text:
Rotate the model key › Steps
1. Create a new key in Google AI Studio at aistudio.google.com/apikey.
2. Replace the `GEMINI_API_KEY` line in `.env`. Never put the key in a source file.
3. Run `./deploy.sh` again. The deploy script copies `.env` into the function's environment variables, so the function only sees the new key after a redeploy.
4. Delete the old key in AI Studio. A deleted key fails with HTTP 400 and the message "API key not valid", which is how you know the old key is gone everywhere.

title: Rotate the model key
heading: Exception
text:
Rotate the model key › Exception
If a classmate's deployment is using your key because theirs was broken on lab night, tell them before you delete the old one. Their function will fail with the same 400 until they redeploy with a key of their own.

title: The first call after a deploy is slow
heading: Symptom
text:
The first call after a deploy is slow › Symptom
The first request after `./deploy.sh`, or the first request after a quiet period, takes three to five seconds. Later requests take about one second. The slow one is a cold start: a new sandbox had to load the runtime, import the SDK, and read the environment before it could run the handler.

title: The first call after a deploy is slow
heading: How to confirm
text:
The first call after a deploy is slow › How to confirm
Look at the `REPORT` line in the function's log. A cold start has an `Init Duration` field; a warm invocation does not. The response body also carries `cold_start: true` and `init_ms`, the time the imports took.

title: The first call after a deploy is slow
heading: What helps
text:
The first call after a deploy is slow › What helps
Keep imports at module level, so they happen once per sandbox and not once per request. Raise the memory with `./deploy.sh --memory 1024`: on this platform more memory is also more CPU, and the import time falls with it. Every sandbox is recycled after some minutes idle, so a service with one request an hour is cold on every request.

title: The first call after a deploy is slow
heading: What does not help
text:
The first call after a deploy is slow › What does not help
Calling the function from a warm-up timer. The timer keeps one sandbox warm; the second concurrent request still gets a cold one. Provisioned concurrency would fix it and is not available in the Learner Lab.

title: The function hits its time limit
heading: Symptom
text:
The function hits its time limit › Symptom
The log shows `Task timed out after 3.00 seconds` (or whatever the limit is) and the caller receives a 502 from the API. The function did not return; the platform killed the process when the limit was reached, and nothing it was doing survived.

title: The function hits its time limit
heading: Why
text:
The function hits its time limit › Why
The time limit is process death. A model call takes one to three seconds warm and longer on a cold start, so a limit of three seconds kills most cold calls and some warm ones. The time limit is set when the function is deployed; the default in `deploy.sh` is 30 seconds.

title: The function hits its time limit
heading: Fix
text:
The function hits its time limit › Fix
Redeploy with a limit that covers a cold start plus a slow model call: `./deploy.sh --timeout 30`. Never set it below 10 seconds for a function that calls the model. If the limit is already 30 and the function still times out, the model is not answering: check RB-01 and RB-07 before raising it further.

title: The function hits its time limit
heading: Related
text:
The function hits its time limit › Related
A request that is killed by the time limit leaves no `INFERENCE` line in the log and no row in the inference table, because the write happens after the model returns. Count the `Task timed out` lines to see how many calls were lost.

title: The API answers 401 or 403
heading: 401 from the HTTP API
text:
The API answers 401 or 403 › 401 from the HTTP API
The route is protected by the shared token. The caller must send the header `x-lab-token` with the value of `LAB_TOKEN` from `.env`. In the Swagger page, click Authorize and paste the token; from curl, add `-H "x-lab-token: ..."`. A missing or wrong token gives `401 bad or missing x-lab-token header`. `GET /` and `/docs` are open and never need the token.

title: The API answers 401 or 403
heading: 403 from a function URL
text:
The API answers 401 or 403 › 403 from a function URL
A bare function URL in the Learner Lab refuses anonymous requests with 403 regardless of its policy. That is why the lab puts an HTTP API in front of the function: the API is reachable with no signature. If you see 403, you are calling the function URL, not the API. Use the URL `deploy.sh` printed, which ends in `execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`.

title: The API answers 401 or 403
heading: A classmate's API
text:
The API answers 401 or 403 › A classmate's API
Use their URL and their token, not yours. The token is checked by their function against their environment, so your token means nothing there.

title: The API answers 429
heading: What it means
text:
The API answers 429 › What it means
A 429 from the API, with no `INFERENCE` line in the log, is the gateway's throttle. The function never ran. The throttle is set per stage with `./deploy.sh --throttle RATE BURST` and removed with `./deploy.sh --throttle off`.

title: The API answers 429
heading: The lag
text:
The API answers 429 › The lag
The setting takes tens of seconds to minutes to reach the edge in both directions, and is applied on a best-effort basis. A storm of requests right after `--throttle 2 5` is usually all 200; a storm right after `--throttle off` can still show some 429. Wait a minute and try again before concluding the setting did not take.

title: The API answers 429
heading: A 429 with an INFERENCE line
text:
The API answers 429 › A 429 with an INFERENCE line
Then the gateway let the request through and the model refused it. That is the provider's rate limit, RB-01, not the gateway's.

title: The API answers 502 or 503
text:
The API answers 502 or 503 › 502
The function crashed or returned something the gateway could not deliver. Look in the log for a `Traceback`, or for `Task timed out` (RB-04). A 502 with `Runtime.ImportModuleError` means the package is missing a dependency: check that `deploy.sh` built the package for the Linux platform and not for your laptop.

title: The API answers 502 or 503
text:
The API answers 502 or 503 › 503
The function ran and gave up on the vendor: a daily quota that is used up, or a provider that keeps returning 5xx. The response body says which. Check the key in `.env` (RB-02) and whether the quota is the daily one (RB-01). Redeploy after fixing `.env`, because the function reads its key from its own environment, not from your laptop.

title: The API answers 502 or 503
heading: 502 from `/chat` only
text:
The API answers 502 or 503 › 502 from `/chat` only
The chat route asks for plain text and the triage route for JSON. A 502 from `/chat` alone, with a `ValidationError` in the log, means the reply did not fit the response model: usually an empty reply from the model after a safety block. Retry once; if it repeats, log the request and move on.

title: The inference table has no rows
heading: Check the log first
text:
The inference table has no rows › Check the log first
Every call writes an `INFERENCE` line to the log before it tries the table. If the lines are there and the rows are not, the write failed and the log has a line beginning `{"level": "warn", "inference_table": ...}` saying why. Common reasons: the table name in the function's `INFERENCES_TABLE` variable does not match, or the LabRole was not attached at creation.

title: The inference table has no rows
heading: Check the day
text:
The inference table has no rows › Check the day
The partition key is the UTC day. After 7 p.m. in Minnesota it is already tomorrow in UTC, so `inferences.py` with no arguments shows an empty day. Use `uv run inferences.py --days 2`.

title: The inference table has no rows
heading: Check the region
text:
The inference table has no rows › Check the region
The table lives in `us-east-1`. A CLI query without `--region us-east-1` looks in whatever region your profile defaults to and finds nothing. The query itself: `aws dynamodb query --table-name triage-inferences --region us-east-1 --key-condition-expression "#d = :d" --expression-attribute-names '{"#d":"day"}' --expression-attribute-values '{":d":{"S":"2026-10-20"}}'`.

title: The inference table has no rows
heading: What a row holds
text:
The inference table has no rows › What a row holds
What happened, never what was said: the time, the route, the build, cold start, latency, the action, the amount, whether the output parsed, and any error. Ticket text is not stored.

title: Reading the function's log
heading: The command
text:
Reading the function's log › The command
`aws logs tail /aws/lambda/triage-api --since 15m --region us-east-1 --format short` shows the last fifteen minutes. Add `--follow` to watch calls land as you make them. Lines arrive a few seconds after the call, and the `REPORT` line arrives last. If the newest call is missing, run the command again.

title: Reading the function's log
heading: One call, line by line
text:
Reading the function's log › One call, line by line
`INIT_START` is written by the platform when a new sandbox starts: the cold start. `START RequestId: ...` is the call beginning; its id is the same one stored in the inference table's row. `INFERENCE {...}` is written by the function: the row as it was written. `END` is the call finishing. `REPORT RequestId: ... Duration ... Billed Duration ... Max Memory Used ... Init Duration` is what the call cost; `Init Duration` appears only on a cold start.

title: Reading the function's log
heading: Following one request
text:
Reading the function's log › Following one request
`aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/lambda/triage-api --region us-east-1 --filter-pattern "REQUEST_ID" --query 'events[].message' --output text` with the id from the row or the `START` line.

title: Reading the function's log
heading: In the console
text:
Reading the function's log › In the console
CloudWatch → Log groups → `/aws/lambda/triage-api` → the newest log stream. One stream per sandbox, so a cold start opens a new stream.

title: The Learner Lab session expired
heading: Symptom
text:
The Learner Lab session expired › Symptom
Every AWS command fails with `ExpiredToken: The security token included in the request is expired`, or `deploy.sh` stops at `sts get-caller-identity failed`. A Learner Lab session lasts about four hours and its credentials die with it.

title: The Learner Lab session expired
heading: Fix
text:
The Learner Lab session expired › Fix
Start the Learner Lab again from the course page, open AWS Details, copy the three credential lines, and paste them over the `[default]` section of `~/.aws/credentials`. Keep the `[default]` header: a file without it fails with `Unable to parse config file`.

title: The Learner Lab session expired
heading: What survives a session ending
text:
The Learner Lab session expired › What survives a session ending
Everything deployed: the function, the HTTP API, the inference table, the bucket, the scheduled rule, and the log groups. They keep working and keep answering requests while the session is off. Only your laptop's credentials expire.

title: The Learner Lab session expired
heading: What does not survive
text:
The Learner Lab session expired › What does not survive
An upload that was in progress. A `deploy.sh` that fails mid-upload with `Connection was closed` had its credentials cancelled under it; start a fresh session and run it again.

title: The nightly scoring run did not fire
heading: Symptom
text:
The nightly scoring run did not fire › Symptom
No new scores file in the bucket this morning, and no `START` line in the batch function's log overnight.

title: The nightly scoring run did not fire
heading: Check the rule
text:
The nightly scoring run did not fire › Check the rule
The run is started by an EventBridge rule named `score-nightly` with a schedule expression such as `cron(0 7 * * ? *)` (07:00 UTC) or, for the lab, `rate(5 minutes)`. Check that the rule's state is `ENABLED`: `aws events describe-rule --name score-nightly --region us-east-1`. A rule created with `schedule.sh --off` is disabled.

title: The nightly scoring run did not fire
heading: Check the target and the permission
text:
The nightly scoring run did not fire › Check the target and the permission
The rule needs a target, the batch function, and the function needs a resource permission for the principal `events.amazonaws.com`. `aws events list-targets-by-rule --rule score-nightly` shows the first; `aws lambda get-policy --function-name score-batch` shows the second. `schedule.sh` creates both; if the function was deleted and recreated, the permission is gone and must be added again.

title: The nightly scoring run did not fire
heading: Rules fire without a session
text:
The nightly scoring run did not fire › Rules fire without a session
The rule fires whether or not your Learner Lab session is running. If it did not fire, the cause is the rule, the target or the permission, never the session.

title: The scores file is missing from the bucket
heading: How a run publishes
text:
The scores file is missing from the bucket › How a run publishes
A run writes its scores file under `runs/<run id>/scores.jsonl`, then runs its check (the row count against the account count, and the score distribution against last night's), and only if the check passes moves the pointer `current.json` to the new run. A run whose check failed leaves its file in place and the pointer where it was.

title: The scores file is missing from the bucket
heading: Diagnosis
text:
The scores file is missing from the bucket › Diagnosis
List the runs: `aws s3 ls s3://<bucket>/runs/`. If today's run directory exists but `current.json` points at yesterday, the check failed; its reason is in the run's `run.json` and in the log. If today's directory does not exist, the run never started: RB-11.

title: The scores file is missing from the bucket
heading: Rerun
text:
The scores file is missing from the bucket › Rerun
`uv run run_batch.py --date 2026-10-20` reruns one date. It is idempotent: the same date produces the same file and replaces it. Do not edit `current.json` by hand; the pointer only moves when a check passes.

title: A score served at the request differs from the stored score
heading: Symptom
text:
A score served at the request differs from the stored score › Symptom
`consistency.py` reports accounts whose score from `/score` differs from the score in last night's file by more than rounding.

title: A score served at the request differs from the stored score
heading: Causes, in order of likelihood
text:
A score served at the request differs from the stored score › Causes, in order of likelihood
The weights file. The function and the batch run each carry `src/model/weights.json` with a `version` field; if the function was deployed from a different commit than the batch run, the two versions differ and so do the scores. Compare the `weights_version` field in the `/score` response with the one in the run's `run.json`.

The features. The batch run joins features as of the run's date; the request path reads the latest features. An account whose features changed today scores differently, and that is correct: the stored score is the account as of last night.

title: A score served at the request differs from the stored score
heading: Fix
text:
A score served at the request differs from the stored score › Fix
Redeploy the function from the same commit as the batch run, then rerun `consistency.py`. Differences that remain should all be accounts whose features changed since the run.

title: deploy.sh fails
heading: `sts get-caller-identity failed`
text:
deploy.sh fails › `sts get-caller-identity failed`
No live session, or credentials not pasted. RB-10.

title: deploy.sh fails
heading: `Connection was closed` during the upload
text:
deploy.sh fails › `Connection was closed` during the upload
The session's credentials were cancelled while the zip was uploading. Start a fresh session, paste credentials, run it again.

title: deploy.sh fails
heading: The zip is too large
text:
deploy.sh fails › The zip is too large
A deployment package must be under 50 MB zipped and 250 MB unpacked, including layers. `deploy.sh` prints both sizes after the build. The usual cause is a dependency that pulled in a large library: check `build/pkg` for anything you did not expect. The model weights for the runbook assistant are data, not a dependency, and are small.

title: deploy.sh fails
heading: `Runtime.ImportModuleError` after a deploy
text:
deploy.sh fails › `Runtime.ImportModuleError` after a deploy
The package was built for the wrong platform. `deploy.sh` installs dependencies with `--python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --python-version 3.12`; if you installed into `build/pkg` by hand from a Mac, the compiled wheels are the Mac ones. Delete `build/` and run `deploy.sh` again.

title: deploy.sh fails
heading: The function exists but the API does not
text:
deploy.sh fails › The function exists but the API does not
`deploy.sh` keeps an existing API and creates one only if none is called `triage-api`. If the API was deleted by `teardown.sh`, the next `deploy.sh` creates it again with a new URL; update `LAB_URL` in `.env`, which the script does for you.

title: The model's output does not parse
heading: What the parser expects
text:
The model's output does not parse › What the parser expects
The triage step asks the model for one JSON object with `action`, `refund_amount` and `rationale`. The parser accepts the object alone or wrapped in a code fence. Anything else, such as `Sure! Here is my decision: refund it.`, is a parse failure and is recorded with `action: "error"`.

title: The model's output does not parse
heading: What to do with a parse failure
text:
The model's output does not parse › What to do with a parse failure
Nothing clever. Count it. The harness reports the parse-failure rate per slice, and it is a rate like any other. A retry at temperature 0 changes the number you measure, so if you retry, record the retry as a second sample, not as a replacement.

title: The model's output does not parse
heading: When the rate jumps
text:
The model's output does not parse › When the rate jumps
A parse-failure rate that was 2% and is now 15% with no change on your side means the vendor changed the model under you. Check the `model` field in the inference rows for a version change, and run the pinned golden set to confirm. Then decide whether to pin the previous version or adjust the prompt; either is a release.

title: Refund limits and who may approve
heading: The limits
text:
Refund limits and who may approve › The limits
A refund of $50 or less is issued by the system itself. A refund above $50 and up to $200 is held for a human to approve. A refund above $200 is escalated to a team lead and is never issued by the system or by a front-line agent.

title: Refund limits and who may approve
heading: Where the limit is enforced
text:
Refund limits and who may approve › Where the limit is enforced
In code, after the model. The model proposes an action and an amount; the validator in the triage function checks the amount against the limits and overrides the action if the model proposed a refund over the cap. A model that says "refund $88" produces a hold, not a refund, whatever its rationale says.

title: Refund limits and who may approve
heading: Exception
text:
Refund limits and who may approve › Exception
Refunds for duplicate charges are issued in full at any amount, by the system, because the money was never the customer's to lose. The duplicate must be confirmed by two orders with the same amount within ten minutes on the same account; the validator checks this, not the model.

title: Refund limits and who may approve
heading: Currency
text:
Refund limits and who may approve › Currency
Limits are in US dollars. An order in another currency is converted at the rate on the order, which is stored on the order row.

title: Escalating a ticket to a person
heading: When
text:
Escalating a ticket to a person › When
Escalate when the model's action is `escalate`, when the validator held a refund above $200, when a customer asks for a person, or when a ticket mentions legal action, the press, or a safety issue.

title: Escalating a ticket to a person
heading: How
text:
Escalating a ticket to a person › How
The escalation writes the ticket to the support queue with the triage record attached: the action proposed, the amount, the rationale, and the request id, so the person can read what the model saw and said. The customer gets an automatic reply saying a person will respond, and nothing else.

title: Escalating a ticket to a person
heading: Service level
text:
Escalating a ticket to a person › Service level
A person responds within four business hours. Business hours are 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Central time, Monday to Friday.

title: Escalating a ticket to a person
heading: Exception
text:
Escalating a ticket to a person › Exception
A ticket that reports a security problem, such as an account the customer did not open or a password they did not change, does not go to the support queue. It goes to the on-call engineer by page, at any hour, and the customer is told within thirty minutes.

title: A customer asks to delete their account
heading: The rule
text:
A customer asks to delete their account › The rule
Account deletion is completed within 30 days of the request. The customer receives a confirmation when the request is logged and a second one when the deletion is done.

title: A customer asks to delete their account
heading: What is deleted
text:
A customer asks to delete their account › What is deleted
The account row, the order history, the ticket text, and the customer's rows in the inference table. The inference table rows are found by the account id in the row, so the deletion job has to read the table; the row's request id is kept in an anonymized form for the audit record.

title: A customer asks to delete their account
heading: Exception
text:
A customer asks to delete their account › Exception
An account with an open refund, a hold awaiting approval, or an escalated ticket cannot be deleted until those are settled. The deletion request is logged, the customer is told why it is waiting, and the 30 days count from the request, not from the settlement.

title: A customer asks to delete their account
heading: Who may do it
text:
A customer asks to delete their account › Who may do it
Only support operations runs the deletion job. Front-line agents log the request and tell the customer.

title: The judge disagrees with you
heading: What the judge is
text:
The judge disagrees with you › What the judge is
A second model call that reads an output and a rubric and answers yes or no. It is a model: it has an error rate, it is nondeterministic, and the vendor changes it.

title: The judge disagrees with you
heading: When you disagree with it
text:
The judge disagrees with you › When you disagree with it
Label thirty outputs yourself, run the judge on the same thirty, and fill in the four counts: both yes, both no, judge yes and you no, judge no and you yes. The judge's sensitivity is the share of your "no" labels it also said no to; its specificity is the share of your "yes" labels it also said yes to. Report both with their counts. Then read every disagreement: judges fail in patterns, and the pattern is what to write into the rubric.

title: The judge disagrees with you
heading: When to do it again
text:
The judge disagrees with you › When to do it again
When the judge's model changed, when the rubric changed, when the system under test started producing a different kind of text, and on a schedule regardless. A judge validated once, against a model that no longer exists, is an opinion.

title: The judge disagrees with you
heading: Its own noise
text:
The judge disagrees with you › Its own noise
Run the judge three times on the same outputs. The share of verdicts that flip is the judge's noise floor, and no difference smaller than that between two versions of the system is a difference.

title: Changing the golden set
heading: The rule
text:
Changing the golden set › The rule
The golden set is versioned. Every change bumps the version in `data/golden/README.md` and the file's hash is recorded with every run that used it. A rate measured on version 3 is not compared with a rate measured on version 4.

title: Changing the golden set
heading: When you add tickets
text:
Changing the golden set › When you add tickets
Add them to a slice, or make a new slice. A ticket without a slice is a ticket whose rate nobody owns. Rerun the noise floor on the slice: three runs of the unchanged system, so the new tickets' variance is known before any change is measured against it.

title: Changing the golden set
heading: When you change an expected answer
text:
Changing the golden set › When you change an expected answer
Write down why, in the ticket's record. If two people disagree about the expected answer, the disagreement is the requirement not yet written; settle it in the policy text first.

title: Changing the golden set
heading: Do not
text:
Changing the golden set › Do not
Do not remove a ticket because the system fails it. A failing ticket is a measurement.

title: Cost and the Learner Lab budget
heading: The budget
text:
Cost and the Learner Lab budget › The budget
The Learner Lab has a fixed $50 budget for the semester and no card behind it. When it is spent, the account stops. A usage alarm at $10 and another at $25 were set on the first day; they send mail to the address on the account.

title: Cost and the Learner Lab budget
heading: What costs nothing while idle
text:
Cost and the Learner Lab budget › What costs nothing while idle
A function, an HTTP API, a DynamoDB table on on-demand pricing, an EventBridge rule, a log group, and a bucket with a few megabytes in it. Leaving the triage service deployed between labs costs nothing measurable.

title: Cost and the Learner Lab budget
heading: What does cost
text:
Cost and the Learner Lab budget › What does cost
Invocations, in tiny amounts; a scheduled rule firing every five minutes for a week, in slightly less tiny amounts; and anything that is not serverless. Do not create EC2 instances, NAT gateways, load balancers or Kubernetes clusters: they are not allowed under the lab role, and one of them running for a weekend would end the budget.

title: Cost and the Learner Lab budget
heading: If the alarm fires
text:
Cost and the Learner Lab budget › If the alarm fires
Find what is running with `aws lambda list-functions`, `aws events list-rules` and the billing console, and disable the schedule with `./schedule.sh --off`.

title: The Swagger page does not open
heading: On the laptop
text:
The Swagger page does not open › On the laptop
The page is at the API's URL with `/docs` on the end, for example `https://abc123.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/docs`. Locally it is `http://127.0.0.1:9000/docs`. A blank page with the URL right usually means the function is returning 502: check the log, RB-07.

title: The Swagger page does not open
heading: On the phone
text:
The Swagger page does not open › On the phone
If the page opens on the laptop and not on the phone, the phone's network is the usual cause: campus guest networks block some hosts. Try mobile data. Copy the URL from the output of `deploy.sh` rather than typing it; the API id is random letters and one wrong character gives a page that never loads.

title: The Swagger page does not open
heading: The Authorize button is missing
text:
The Swagger page does not open › The Authorize button is missing
The token header is declared as an API key in the app so that Swagger shows the button. If the button is missing, the deployed code is older than the one on your laptop: run `./deploy.sh` again.

title: The queue is backing up
heading: Symptom
text:
The queue is backing up › Symptom
Tickets wait more than fifteen minutes between arrival and triage. The queue depth climbs and does not come down.

title: The queue is backing up
heading: Why adding workers does not help
text:
The queue is backing up › Why adding workers does not help
The consumer is bounded by the model's per-minute rate, not by compute. More consumer functions produce more 429s from the provider and the same throughput. The queue is the shock absorber: it holds work until the model can take it.

title: The queue is backing up
heading: What to do
text:
The queue is backing up › What to do
First check whether the model is refusing (RB-01): a backlog that started at the same moment as a run of 429s is the provider's rate limit, and the fix is to wait or to use a key with a higher limit. Then check the consumer's reserved concurrency; a value of 1 serializes every ticket. Raise it to the number of requests per minute the key allows, divided by the per-ticket latency in minutes.

title: The queue is backing up
heading: During a vendor outage
text:
The queue is backing up › During a vendor outage
Do not scale. Let the queue hold the tickets; set the customer-facing reply to "we have your ticket" and let the backlog drain when the model is back. Tickets older than four hours in the queue are escalated to the support queue by the age rule, so nobody waits forever.

title: Calling a classmate's API
heading: What you need from them
text:
Calling a classmate's API › What you need from them
Their API URL, which ends in `execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`, and their `LAB_TOKEN`. Do not ask for their Gemini key; it stays in their function.

title: Calling a classmate's API
heading: From the terminal
text:
Calling a classmate's API › From the terminal
`LAB_URL=https://THEIRS.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/triage LAB_TOKEN=THEIR_TOKEN ./call.sh` sends one ticket to their function. Their function writes the row to their inference table and the line to their log, not yours.

title: Calling a classmate's API
heading: From the Swagger page
text:
Calling a classmate's API › From the Swagger page
Open their URL with `/docs`, click Authorize, paste their token, and send a `POST /chat`.

title: Calling a classmate's API
heading: If theirs is down
text:
Calling a classmate's API › If theirs is down
Their Learner Lab session being off does not take the API down; the function answers without a session. If it is down, their function or key is broken, and the symptoms are the same as for your own: RB-05 for 401, RB-07 for 502 and 503.
